question: According to the ILAE 2014 definition, epilepsy can be diagnosed after a SINGLE unprovoked seizure if the risk of a second seizure over the next 10 years is 60% or greater.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is true. The ILAE 2014 definition allows epilepsy to be diagnosed after just one unprovoked seizure if the 10-year recurrence risk is ≥60%. This reflects biological certainty of recurring seizures — for example, after a structural brain lesion on MRI or a clearly epileptogenic EEG pattern. Previously, two unprovoked seizures were required; the new definition reflects evidence-based risk stratification.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. The ILAE 2014 operational definition of epilepsy includes: (1) at least two unprovoked seizures more than 24 hours apart, OR (2) one unprovoked seizure with a probability of further seizures ≥60% over the next 10 years (equivalent to the recurrence risk after two unprovoked seizures), OR (3) diagnosis of an epilepsy syndrome. This updated definition allows treatment to begin after a single seizure when the recurrence risk is clearly high.
